Title: Resignation from the United States Senate - Wikipedia

Main.id: Resignation from the United States Senate - Wikipedia#1
Main.sentence: A member of the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ can ___E:resign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resignation)___ by writing a letter of resignation to the ___E:governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States))___ of the state that the senator represents.

Main.id: Resignation from the United States Senate - Wikipedia#2
Main.sentence: Under ___E:Article I, Section 3 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_One_of_the_United_States_Constitution#Section_3:_Senate)___ of the ___E:Constitution of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States)___ , and under the ___E:Seventeenth Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ , in case of a vacancy in the Senate resulting from resignation, the executive authority of the state (today known in every state as the governor) can make a temporary appointment to fill the vacancy if so authorized by the state legislature.

Main.id: Resignation from the United States Senate - Wikipedia#3
Main.sentence: A special election may follow depending on timing and state law. Whenever a senator needs to be appointed or elected, the ___E:Secretary of the Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_the_Senate)___ mails one of three forms to the state's governor to inform that person of the proper wording to certify the appointment of a new Senator.

Main.id: Resignation from the United States Senate - Wikipedia#4
Main.sentence: The first resignation from the Senate was that of ___E:William Paterson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Paterson_(judge))___ of New Jersey on November 13, 1790, who resigned in order to accept the office of ___E:Governor of New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_Jersey)___ . [citation needed] His resignation was only the third time a person ceased to hold a seat in the Senate, which had first convened during the preceding year, 1789. The earlier ones resulted from the death of Senator ___E:William Grayson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Grayson)___ of ___E:Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia)___ , and the expiration of the term of the temporary senator ___E:John Walker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Walker_(Virginia_politician))___ of Virginia, who was appointed by the ___E:Governor of Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Virginia)___ to hold that office until a successor could be elected in November. [citation needed]

Main.id: Resignation from the United States Senate - Wikipedia#5
Resignation from the United States Senate - Wikipedia#6
Main.sentence: Nine senators resigned during that year—a record-high number that stands to this day. [citation needed] Most resignations have been motivated either by declining health or a decision to accept another office. [citation needed] Sixteen persons have resigned from the Senate twice and two have resigned three times. [citation needed]
